## Q1. How many Sars-Cov-2 papers?

### 1.0. Downloading the website

```{r}
website <- xml2::read_html(
  "https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/?term=sars-cov-2"
)
```

### 1.1. Locate the result count and convert it to text

```{r}
counts <- xml2::xml_find_first(
  website,
  "//div[contains(@class, 'results-amount')]//span[@class='value']"
)
counts <- as.character(counts)
```

### 1.2. Extract data and clean the outputs 

```{r}
totalcount <- stringr::str_extract(counts, "[0-9]+([,.][0-9]+)*")

totalcount <- gsub("[,.]", "", totalcount)

totalcount <- as.numeric(totalcount)
print(totalcount)
```

## Q2. Get article abstracts and authors 

```{r}
# Read the abstract file
abstracts <- readLines(
  "~/Downloads/abstract-sars-cov-2-set.txt",
  warn = FALSE
)

# Inspect the first 20 lines
head(abstracts, 20)
```

```{r}
# Combine all lines into one string
abstracts <- paste(abstracts, collapse = "\n")

# Split the text into individual articles
abstracts <- unlist(strsplit(abstracts, split = "\n\n\n"))

# Replace remaining line breaks with spaces
abstracts <- gsub("\n", " ", abstracts)

# Replace multiple spaces with a single space
abstracts <- gsub(" +", " ", abstracts)
```

```{r}
# Number of entries
length(abstracts)

# Inspect the first two entries
abstracts[1:2]
```

## Q3. Distribution of universities 

### 3.1. Extract institution names 

```{r}
library(stringr)

# Combine patterns for the three institution formats
institution_pattern <- paste(
  c(
    "[A-Z][a-zA-Z'-]*( [A-Z][a-zA-Z'-]*)* University",
    "University of [A-Z][a-zA-Z'-]*( [A-Z][a-zA-Z'-]*)*",
    "[A-Z][a-zA-Z'-]*( [A-Z][a-zA-Z'-]*)* Institute of [A-Z][a-zA-Z'-]*( [A-Z][a-zA-Z'-]*)*"
  ),
  collapse = "|"
)

# Extract all matching institutions from each article
institution <- str_extract_all(
  abstracts,
  institution_pattern
)
```

### 3.2. Inspect the extracted institutions 

```{r}
# Check institutions extracted from the first two articles
institution[1:2]
```

### 3.3. Count and rank institutions

```{r}
# Combine the extracted names into one vector
institution <- unlist(institution)

# Count occurrences and sort from highest to lowest
institution_counts <- sort(
  table(institution),
  decreasing = TRUE
)

# Show the 10 most common institutions
top10 <- head(institution_counts, 10)
top10
```

The 10 most common institution names in my results were:

1.  University of California: 4,358

2.  Stanford University: 1,171

3.  University of Southern California: 786

4.  University of California San Francisco: 701

5.  University of California San Diego: 682

6.  The University: 398

7.  University of Washington: 338

8.  Columbia University: 274

9.  University of California Los Angeles: 254

10. Johns Hopkins University: 246

I noticed that “The University” appeared 398 times, but this does not tell us which university it is. To improve the results, I could remove matches that are only “The University”. I could also check a few extracted names against the original author affiliations. If a name is incomplete or includes extra words, I could adjust the regular expression to capture it more accurately.

## Q4. Make a tidy dataset 

### 4.1. 

```{r}
# read in text, each line is a separate character
abstracts <- readLines(
  "~/Downloads/abstract-sars-cov-2-set.txt",
  warn = FALSE
)

# combine all text into one character
abstracts <- paste(abstracts, collapse = "\n")

# split the text whenever 3 new lines occur in a row
abstracts <- unlist(strsplit(abstracts, split = "\n\n\n"))

# Inspect the first article with line breaks displayed
cat(abstracts[1])
```

### 4.2. Extract journal names

```{r}
# Extract the journal name before the publication year
journal <- str_extract(
  abstracts,
  "(?<=\\. ).+?(?=\\. [0-9]{4})"
)

# Inspect the first five journal names
journal[1:5]
```

### 4.3. Extract article titles 

```{r}
# Extract the second paragraph from each article
titles <- sapply(abstracts, function(x) {
  unlist(strsplit(x, split = "\n\n"))[2]
}, USE.NAMES = FALSE)

# Replace line breaks within titles with spaces
titles <- gsub("\n", " ", titles)

# Inspect the first five titles
titles[1:5]
```

### 4.4. Extract article authors

```{r}
# Extract the third paragraph from each article
authors <- sapply(abstracts, function(x) {
  unlist(strsplit(x, split = "\n\n"))[3]
}, USE.NAMES = FALSE)

# Replace line breaks within author lists with spaces
authors <- gsub("\n", " ", authors)

# Inspect the first five author lists
authors[1:5]
```

###  4.5. Extract author affiliations 

```{r}
# Extract the text after "Author information:"
# Stop at the next blank line
affiliations <- str_extract(
  abstracts,
  "(?<=Author information:\\n)[\\s\\S]+?(?=\\n\\n)"
)

# Replace line breaks within affiliations with spaces
affiliations <- gsub("\n", " ", affiliations)

# Replace multiple spaces with a single space
affiliations <- gsub(" +", " ", affiliations)

# Inspect the first five affiliations
affiliations[1:5]
```

###  4.6. Create the tidy dataset

```{r}
# Combine the extracted information
papers <- data.frame(
  journal = journal,
  title = titles,
  authors = authors,
  affiliations = affiliations
)

# Display the first five papers
knitr::kable(papers[1:5, ])
```
